chunks.arabic_text: غَيْبَةُ الطُّوسِيِّ: جَمَاعَةٌ، عَنْ أَبِي مُحَمَّدٍ هَارُونَ بْنِ مُوسَى، عَنْ أَبِي عَلِيٍّ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ هَمَّامٍ الْإِسْكَافِيِّ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ الْحِمْيَرِيِّ، عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ سَعْدٍ الْقُمِّيِّ قَالَ

translations.en: Ghayba of al-Tusi: A group, from Abi Muhammad Harun ibn Musa, from Abi Ali Muhammad ibn Hammam al-Iskafi, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq ibn Sa'd al-Qummi, who said:

chunks.arabic_text: دَخَلْتُ عَلَى أَبِي الْحَسَنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ صَلَوَاتُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ فِي يَوْمٍ مِنَ الْأَيَّامِ فَقُلْتُ: يَا سَيِّدِي أَنَا أَغِيبُ وَأَشْهَدُ وَلَا يَتَهَيَّأُ لِي الْوُصُولُ إِلَيْكَ إِذَا شَهِدْتُ فِي كُلِّ وَقْتٍ، فَقَوْلُ مَنْ نَقْبَلُ؟ وَأَمْرُ مَنْ نَمْتَثِلُ؟ فَقَالَ لِي: هَذَا أَبُو عَمْرٍو الثِّقَةُ الْأَمِينُ مَا قَالَ لَكُمْ فَعَنِّي يَقُولُهُ، وَمَا أَدَّى إِلَيْكُمْ فَعَنِّي يُؤَدِّيهِ. فَلَمَّا مَضَى أَبُو الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ وَصَلْتُ إِلَى أَبِيهِ مُحَمَّدِ الْحَسَنِ الْعَسْكَرِيِّ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ مِثْلَ قَوْلِي لِأَبِيهِ، فَقَالَ لِي: هَذَا أَبُو عَمْرٍو الثِّقَةُ الْأَمِينُ ثِقَةُ الْمَاضِي وَثِقَتِي فِي الْمَحْيَا وَالْمَمَاتِ، فَمَا قَالَ لَكُمْ فَعَنِّي يَقُولُهُ، وَمَا أَدَّى إِلَيْكُمْ فَعَنِّي يُؤَدِّيهِ

translations.en: I entered to see Abi al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) one day and said: O my master, I am sometimes absent and at other times present, and it is not feasible for me to reach you when I am present at every time, so whose words do we accept? And whose orders do we follow? He said to me: This is Abu Amr, the trustworthy and dependable; whatever he says to you, he is saying it on my behalf, and whatever he conveys to you, he is conveying it on my behalf. When Abi al-Hasan (peace be upon him) passed away, I went to his son Abi Muhammad al-Hasan al-Askari (peace be upon him) one day and said to him the same as I had said to his father, so he said to me: This is Abu Amr, the trustworthy and dependable, the trustee of the one who has passed and my trustee in life and death; whatever he says to you, he is saying it on my behalf, and whatever he conveys to you, he is conveying it on my behalf.

en.summary: This hadith from al-Hasan al-Mufid's *Ghaybat al-Tusi* establishes the doctrine of *al-Tawqi'* (the specific decree) regarding the transition from the Minor to the Major Occultation, identifying Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Amri as the definitive deputy (*na'ib al-sadiq*). The Imams' affirmation that 'what he says is what I say' underscores the continuity of religious authority and the binding nature of his rulings during the Imam's absence, a cornerstone of Twelver Shia jurisprudence.
en.seo_question: Who was the trustworthy deputy of the Imams during the period of absence according to al-Tusi's Ghayba?

key_terms.فَعَنِّي يَقُولُهُ: He says it on my behalf
key_terms.فَعَنِّي يُؤَدِّيهِ: He conveys it on my behalf
key_terms.ثِقَةُ الْمَاضِي: Trustee of the one who has passed
key_terms.ثِقَتِي فِي الْمَحْيَا وَالْمَمَاتِ: My trustee in life and death
